$comment: Schema/contract for the custom-proposal template. The build step replaces {{LEAD_JSON}} in template.html with one JSON object matching this shape. Every field below lists: path, type, description, and the Remote-Guyana worked-example value (base64 data URIs truncated to 'data:image/...;base64,<...>'). Inline HTML (e.g. <b>) is allowed only in fields marked (html); other text fields are plain text. For ALL text you may write literal Unicode (em-dash, &, apostrophes) OR HTML entities — build.py decodes entities so both render correctly. Do NOT put tags in non-(html) fields. caseStudies/opportunities are the GigRadar-library + market data; everything else is lead-specific.

serviceTags.desc: TOP-LEVEL. The lead's service niches, from the case-studies taxonomy (lead-gen, cold-email, email-marketing, revops, crm, data-analytics, web-development, software-development, mobile-development, design-ux, ecommerce, ai-automation, no-code, ppc-ads, seo, content, video-creative, bookkeeping-finance, va-admin-support, customer-support, bpo-staffing, market-research, marketing-agency, consulting, automation). build.py uses these to auto-select the most relevant case studies by tag overlap — set 3-6 that best describe the lead. Tag generously; sparse tags make the grid fall back to library order.

proposalTool.$comment: Section 7 — the interactive 'watch the proposal write itself' block, placed just before the final CTA. Generated by a DEDICATED sub-agent (Sonnet, KB-equipped) — see references/proposal-tool.md. Left = the GigRadar cover letter with a 3-way tone switch (Formal/Quirky/Creative); right = the live Upwork job with a job switch. Changing the job re-renders BOTH sides; changing the tone re-renders only the letter. You must supply n jobs × 3 tones = 3n letters (n = the same jobs as twinsSection.twins, usually 4). Every string field here is HTML-capable (build.py unescapes entities).

headline.example: Every job gets its own proposal — written to convert, in your voice.

intro.example: This is the exact thing your future clients feel on the other end. Pick any live job on the right and GigRadar drafts the cover letter on the left — grounded in 133K proposals of what actually earns replies.

explainer.desc: Plain-language 'what is this' callout so a reader who has NEVER used Upwork understands the tool. Explain job-post → proposal → reply in one short paragraph.
explainer.example: New to how Upwork works? Companies post a job (right). Freelancers send a short written proposal (left) to win it — that letter is the entire first impression, and most are generic and ignored. GigRadar's AI writes a tailored one for every matching job in your voice, then sends it for you.

foot.desc: Dark footer strip tying the tool to conversion. Start with a … pill, then a sentence with the reply-rate proof and an … link.
foot.example: ⚡ Auto-written & sent Every GigRadar client gets a proposal like this drafted and sent for each matching job, automatically — that's why our agencies reply at 12–18% vs the 4% Upwork median. See it write one live →

jobs.desc: The n jobs (usually the same 4 as twinsSection.twins). Each carries the job details (right side) + 3 tone-specific letters (left side).

tabLabel.desc: VERY short label for the job-switch pill — 1–2 words, ≤ ~12 chars, so all n pills fit on one row (e.g. 'Webflow', 'Shopify+', 'React UI', 'Headless'). The switch wraps gracefully if longer, but short is cleaner.

jobStats.desc: Budget + client-quality chips. {v} is the bold value, {k} the caption; set {ver:true} for a green 'verified' style chip (renders a ✓). Put the budget first, e.g. {v:'$15–45',k:'/hr'}.

jobSkills.desc: Skill chips shown on the job.

jobDescription.desc:
What the client wrote — 1–2 short

(a

    of requirements is fine). Keep it real and skimmable.

letters.desc: EXACTLY three keys (formal, quirky, creative), each a distinct cover letter for THIS job. Same offer/proof across tones; only the voice changes. See references/proposal-tool.md for the tone definitions, the hard rules (no long dashes, no 'KB', no fabrication), and knowledge-base grounding.

coverLetter.desc:
The letter as HTML: first

, body

s, final

. ~90-140 words. Open on the CLIENT'S outcome (never 'I am writing to apply'); include one concrete, REAL proof (from the lead's dossier, never invented); end with ONE low-friction CTA. NO long dashes (em/en) anywhere; sign off with no leading dash.
coverLetter.example:
Hi there,

You need CRM-ready B2B data your team actually trusts.

Satiesh, Remote Guyana

whyConverts.desc: 2-3 short bullets naming WHY this letter converts (the persuasion mechanics).
example: Opens on the client's outcome, not a bio
Cites a real, sourced number (5.3x reply lift for their client Clay BPO)

kbSourced.desc: 2-3 short bullets citing the REAL knowledge-base pattern each move is grounded in, and how it was made specific to this lead/job. Say 'knowledge base' / 'our proposal data' / 'insights from 133,872 proposals' — NEVER the abbreviation 'KB'. Cite real insights only.
example: First line mirrors the job's own words, our proposal data shows top-decile letters get specific in sentence one
Leads with one real, sourced result rather than a generic pitch

quirky.desc: The quirky-tone letter (same shape as formal: coverLetter, whyConverts, kbSourced).

creative.desc: The creative-tone letter (same shape as formal: coverLetter, whyConverts, kbSourced).

caseStudies.desc: GigRadar case-study cards (the dark grid near the bottom). Rendered by the CASES map. Content is GigRadar's library, not lead-specific, but still injected so it can be curated per lead.
